Come, child! My beauty, come—
Come and dance us some new dance!
[Esmeralda prepares to dance, and draws from her bosom the scarf which Phœbus gave her.

My scarf! Phœbus, you have deceived me!
My rival! Here she is!
[Fleur-de-lys snatches the scarf from Esmeralda , and falls in a swoon. All the people rush angrily toward the gypsy, who flies for protection to Phœbus .

lg.l: Is it true that Phœbus loves her?
To brave us thus in our own home,
You must have an audacious heart.
Go back into the public street!
The common tradesmen, they can praise
The jumping of your low-born feet.
Away with her, away at once!
Out at the door! 'Tis a disgrace
For this degraded girl to lift
Her eyes to such a lofty place.
Oh, defend me! Help! Defend me,
Save me, Phœbus, I implore thee;
I love her, and I love but her.
Yes! her defender I will be.
I'll fight for her, and my strong arm
Will bear my heart out valiantly.
If some one must be her protector,
I am the one—and doubt me not,
Her wrongs are mine, and who insults her
Must answer for it on the spot.
What! She is what he loves! Indeed!
Away from here, away from here!
A gypsy he prefers to us;
With loving words he calms her fear.
Hush! silence! Both of you be still!

div.p:
[To Phœbus .] From you, 'tis too much arrogance!
[To Esmeralda .] From thee, too much impertinence!
[Phœbus and his friends protect the gypsy, who is menaced by all the guests of Madame De Gondelaurier . Esmeralda staggers toward the door.

Scene.—The front yard of a tavern. Tavern to the right; trees to the left. In the back a door, and a small low wall which closes in the yard. In the distance the roof of Notre Dame with its towers and its spire. A dark silhouette of old Paris outlines itself against the red sunset. The river Seine is at the base of the picture

p.hi: , seated at tables, are drinking, and singing; afterward

lg.l: To him who only water hates
Rocks the canvas of his tent
To him who only water hates

div.p: [Enter Claude Frollo , who seats himself at a table at some distance from Phœbus , and appears at first to observe nothing that passes around him.

That pretty gypsy,
What are you doing with her?
[Claude Frollo makes a movement of attention.

To-night, in an hour,
I have a meeting with her.

lg.l: To feel one heart holds two!
To own the woman that one loves—
To have her soul; to have her charms,
Her song which fills with bliss;
To see her sweet eyes wet with tears,
To dry them with a kiss.

div.p: [While he sings, the others drink and strike their glasses.

lg.l: And to love what one drinks!

div.p:
I bind myself to hell;
Misfortune on you dwell!

lg.l: I'd give a century for an hour,

div.p: [The curfew rings; the friends of Phœbus arise from the table, replace their swords, their caps, their cloaks, and prepare to depart.

lg.l: At last the hour is come;

p.hi: as he is about to go out

div.p:
Do you know the name of the one
Who awaits you at the meeting to-night?

lg.l: By my life, it is my beauty!
The one I love and who loves me.

div.p:
Friend! First, you are an idiot;
Second, go to the devil!
Phœbus, if you cross the threshold of that door—

lg.l: Tremble! One of the gypsies she!
No law protects those awful places.
There love's a masquerade for hate,
Death lies concealed in their embraces.
My dear sir, readjust your cape,
Strange they allow you to escape!
Believe that the report speaks true.
Darkness strange and deep surrounds them;
Phœbus! there death waits for you!

div.p: [Claude Frollo's earnestness seems to trouble Phœbus , who looks at his interrogator with anxiety.

lg.l: In spite of myself, with doubt!
In spite of himself, with doubt.
Believe me—my lord, avoid the siren
More than one gypsy in her rage
Has stabbed a heart palpitating with love.

div.p: [Phœbus , whom he tries to drag along, recovers himself and pushes him off.

lg.l: The love that questions what she be
Is love most base and poor.
If death be but as sweet as she,
It will be fine to die!

div.p: [Phœbus exits quickly, in spite of Claude Frollo . Claude Frollo stands gloomy and undecided for a moment; then follows Phœbus .

p.hi: A chamber. In the background, a window which opens on the river.

enters, bearing a torch. He is followed by several men, to whom he makes a preconcerted sign, and places them in a dark corner, in which they disappear; then he returns to the door and signals to some one to come up.

div.p:
From here you can see the captain
And the gypsy without being seen.
[He shows him an alcove behind some tapestry.
The men are stationed and ready?

lg.l: The projector of this must never be known.
I will give you as much more afterward.

div.p: [Claude Frollo hides himself in the alcove. Clopin exits with caution. Esmeralda and Phœbus enter.

lg.l: My feelings I try to hide.
My heart is filled with shame,
I beg you blush no more.

div.p: [Phœbus makes Esmeralda sit down on the bench beside him.

The adorable creature!
Upon my soul, you are divine!

lg.l: I beg of you, don't come so near.

div.p: They love each other. How I envy them!
My Phœbus! I owe my life to you.
And I—I owe my happiness to you.

lg.l: Such is my love for thee!
My blade must have its turn.
Be always white and red, my love,
And smile at our bright lot;
Smile sweet at love, which we've awaked,
Your mouth is heaven—my heaven, love—
My soul would cling in bliss
Upon it, love, and pray that life
Might end with one long kiss.
Your voice delights my ear, love;
Your smile is sweet and free.
The laughing passion in your eyes
Your wishes are my law, love,
But I can't yield to this:
Might die in that long kiss!
Don't let them hear your step, Death,
As near to them you creep!
My jealous hatred will keep watch
From out their arms so closely locked
You die for that long kiss!

div.p: [Claude Frollo rushes upon Phœbus and stabs him; then he opens the window in the back, through which he escapes. With a great cry, Esmeralda falls upon the body of Phœbus . The men stationed at the corner rush forward, seize her, and seem to accuse her.
Scene.—A prison. Door in the center
ESMERALDA (alone, chained, lying upon a bed of straw).

lg.l: What! He in the tomb and I in this cell—
He a victim and I a prisoner!
I saw him fall! In truth, he's dead!
And this crime, this awful crime—
They say it is my work!
The stem of our life, while yet green, is broken.
Phœbus has gone, and he shows me the way.
No help given, to those bereft
God in heaven, I adore thee!
Deign to end my life to-day
Or to take my love away!
Phœbus, let us turn our wings
Where all things must go at last,
Where love bides and is eternal.
On earth our bodies sleep together,
In heaven our souls will live forever!
God in heaven, I adore thee!
Deign to end my life to-day
Or to take my love away!

div.p: [The door opens. Claude Frollo enters, a lamp in his hand, his hood pulled over his face: he comes and stands, motionless, in front of Esmeralda .
Will it be soon? Answer me, father!

Perhaps I, who shall live to-morrow,
Suffer more than you.

lg.l: It is the priest! O God! my feeble strength inspire!
It is indeed his brow of ice, it is his glance of fire!
'Tis he who has pursued me, remorseless, day and night;
'Twas he who killed my Phœbus, and slew my heart's delight.
Monster, from my prison, with death's cold hand on me,
I'll curse thee, till within the grave my lips shall silent be!
What have I done to thee? What is thine awful plan?
What dost thou want with me, relentless, impious man?
This love, it is my soul;
This love, it is my blood!

div.p:
Pity me. I love you! Your pity I implore!
For you I've sinned. Have mercy, do not curse me more!

He loves me! Oh, crown of horrors!
He holds me—this horrible sorcerer!

lg.l: The only living thing in me
Is my love and my anguish!
She shudders, quivers in my arms;
The priest has won his chance at last!
By night I bore her, once, away;
Now, in the day, I'll hold her fast!
Death, which follows in my train,
Will give her back to love again!
Phœbus is dead; he waits above.
I shiver at your frightful love,
E'en as the bird which, tortured, dies

div.p:
Accept me, I love you! Refuse me no more!
Have pity for me, for yourself, I implore!

Hush! your impious words!
Your love makes death beautiful!
Choose! choose! Or Claude or death!
[Claude falls at Esmeralda's feet in supplication. She repels him.

lg.l: No, murderer, I will not! Hush!
A crime is this foul love you've nursed.
Better the tomb to which I fly—
Be cursed amid the most accursed!
Tremble, for the scaffold claims you!
You know not what awful schemes
This breast of fury has engendered;
And hell abets me in my dreams.
Ah! since in vain I supplicate,
In vain thy hate I fight,
To God my love leads me:
The gates of heaven he'll open,
But hell shall close o'er thee!

div.p: [A jailer appears. Claude Frollo signs to him to lead out Esmeralda . He exits while they drag forth the gypsy.

p.hi: The area before Notre Dame; the front of the church. The sound of bells is heard

div.p: [He turns toward the front of the church.

lg.l: I saw black hangings in the chapel.
Are they dragging some misery here?
God! a presentiment! I'll not believe it!

div.p: [Enter Claude Frollo and Clopin without perceiving Quasimodo .
It is my master! I'll observe him. He is gloomy too!
[He hides himself in an obscure angle of the porch.

Oh, my mistress! Oh, Notre Dame!
Take my life! save my soul!
My lord, he is not dead!

lg.l: He is too feeble yet for such a journey.
If he came, 'twould be his death.
My lord, you can feel sure
That every step would reopen his wound;
Do not fear anything this morning.
Oh! let me hold her just to-day
For life or death within my power!
Hell! I'll give you all the rest,
If you grant me this one hour!
[To Clopin .] They will soon bring the gypsy here!

div.p:
Keep in the shadow;
If I cry, "To me!" you come.

I rush to her,
I tear her from the King's men—

Hide your arms,
Not to excite suspicion!

lg.l: But hell may take her quick,
On this my only chance I wait
And on this last and only chance

div.p: [They go out hurriedly. The populace begin to enter the square.

p.hi: , priests, archers, officers of the law

div.p: [The crowd increases; noise; a gloomy procession begins to appear on the Place du Parvis. Rows of black penitents. Banners of La Miséricorde. Torches, archers, officers of the law and the watch. The soldiers disperse the crowd. Esmeralda appears. She wears a chemise; a rope is around her neck; her feet are bare, and she is covered with a long black veil of crape. Following her, come the executioners and the King's officers. As the prisoner reaches the front of the church, a somber chant is heard in the distance, coming from the interior of the church, whose doors are closed.

[The chant draws nearer. It bursts forth, at length, when near the doors, which open suddenly and discover the interior of the church. It is filled with a long procession of priests in their robes of ceremony; banners are borne before them. Claude Frollo , in sacerdotal costume, leads the procession. He goes toward the criminal.

Alive to-day, to-morrow dead!
Heaven! thy wings around her spread!

lg.l: It is Phœbus who calls me
Where God will hold us in His arms,
Though plunged in the abyss of woe,
I am to die upon the earth
To die so young, so beautiful!
Must suffer greater woe than she;
You only die from off this earth,
While heaven is lost to me!
Say that in heaven for such as she
Death holds her fast, what misery!
She dies unto the world this day,
Yes, it is I! I love you, I entreat you!
Say but one word! 'Tis not too late;

div.p: Then die! I'll go where I can find you!

lg.l: We deliver this woman to the secular arm;
At this solemn moment may the breath of the Lord

div.p: [As the officers of the law are about to seize Esmeralda , Quasimodo jumps into the square, thrusts back the archers, takes Esmeralda in his arms, and throws himself with her into the church.
CLAUDE FROLLO (commanding silence by a gesture).

lg.l: She is not saved! She is a gypsy!
Notre Dame can save none but Christians!
Pagans are proscribed even when clasping the altar!
[To the King's men.] In the name of my lord the Archbishop of Paris,
I give you back this sinful woman!

div.p:
I will defend her! I swear it.
Approach us not!

lg.l: Tear the gypsy from this holy place.

div.p: [The archers advance. Quasimodo places himself between them and Esmeralda .
[A horseman is heard approaching. He calls out:
PHŒBUS (appearing on horseback. He is pale, breathless, exhausted as is a man who has made a long journey).

The priest alone is guilty, and I will prove it!
Arrest him!
My adored Phœbus, we shall live!

lg.l: At thy feet receive me, humble girl!
Heavens! thou art pale! What is the matter?

div.p: [She catches him in her arms. Expectation and anxiety among the crowd.

lg.l: Each step I took toward you, my beloved,
Reopened my wound, that was hardly healed.
I have taken your grave and given you life.
I die! Destiny has avenged thee.
My angel, I go to see
If heaven is worth thy love!

div.p: Phœbus! He dies! In an instant everything is changed!
